svg.title: States a durable fiber moves through, including the retry ladder
svg.desc: A manifest with spec.execution.mode durable answers POST /chat with 202 and a resume token instead of running the turn inline. The fiber row starts pending; each worker's fiber loop polls every second and claims due rows under a lease, with the one-minute fiber_scheduler sweep as a backstop, oldest first, so two replicas cannot run the same step and no tenant starves; each step either advances the cursor or parks the fiber for a backoff. The backoff doubles from one minute to a ceiling of one hour, and after FELIX_FIBER_MAX_ATTEMPTS consecutive failures the fiber is buried as dead rather than retried forever. The row reads pending while the 202 and the run_accepted frame report the run as accepted. stop_fiber ends a fiber nothing wants any more as failed; one a worker already holds keeps its invoke, but the worker's save loses the compare-and-set and the stopped status stands. A cancelled stream is the client's own report, not a fiber status. A step that reached a terminal status and then failed only at its save keeps that status, because coercing it back to sleeping would re-enter the step loop with the cursor past the end and report a failed invoke as completed.
